title: Customer request orchestration: network gating and compatibility rubric for Private/VPC/on‑prem
creator: Maya Chen
description: Purpose: define a repeatable orchestration and decision rubric for triaging non-bug customer requests for Private / VPC / on‑prem deployments where networking, upgrade windows, or air‑gapped constraints drive complexity. This doc codifies gate checks, minimum artifacts to progress, risk scoring, and the fast‑lane/standard/backlog lanes so PMs and Solutions can consistently route requests and set expectations. Scope: new private deployment requests, major network changes from existing private customers, upgrade timeline exceptions, and air‑gap readiness inquiries. Out of scope: feature requests unrelated to deployment topology, incident remediation for live production outages (use incident process).
decision_rubric: Gate 0 - Completeness: request has customer contact, account ID, environment type (VPC / on‑prem), approximate peak QPS, and whether customer controls KMS/HSM.

Gate 1 - Network Readiness: run lightweight probe checklist (egress endpoints, NAT rules, allowed ports, DNS resolution) and score 0-5. If score <=2, route to 'Network Remediation' with template playbook; if score >=4, continue.

Gate 2 - Upgrade & Window Constraints: capture allowed maintenance windows, blackout dates, approval authority. If customer requires simultaneous on‑prem upgrade across N nodes with zero‑downtime and we lack automation, mark as 'High operational risk'.

Gate 3 - Air‑gap Constraints: enumerate data flow requirements (model artifacts, telemetry, telemetry opt‑out), offline signing needs, and KMS/HSM integration surface. If artifacts >100GB or tooling requires outbound blob access, require engineering feasibility spike.
Gate 4 - SLA & Commercial Fit: map the request to revenue and contract tier. Fast‑lane eligible if ARR > $250k or strategic referenceability AND technical gates pass with low remediation effort.

Score aggregation: normalize gate scores into a 0-100 risk score. Thresholds: 0-30 (Fast‑lane), 31-65 (Standard pipeline + estimated remediation), 66-100 (Escalate to Enterprise ops for bespoke runway).
Outcome decisions: each lane has predefined SLA for PM acknowledgement, Solutions intake call, and engineering feasibility spike timelines.
required_artifacts: Customer intake form (link to form) with contact, env type, maintenance windows, and expected throughput
Network diagram (customer-provided) or completed network probe checklist CSV
Security posture snapshot: KMS/HSM provider, internal PKI constraints, and compliance notes
Binary size estimate for model blobs and registry access constraints
Existing contract or procurement window (if applicable)
comms_playbook: Initial ack: PM sends templated acknowledgement within 1 business day with required artifacts checklist
Triage call: schedule 1-hour intake with Solutions + Customer Engineering within 3 business days for Standard lane, 24 hours for Fast‑lane
Weekly updates: for active remediation tracks, publish concise status notes to customer and internal channel every 5 business days
Escalation: if score >66, loop in Head of Enterprise & Security for decision within 72 hours
acceptance_criteria: All required artifacts submitted and validated (Gate 0 completed)
Network probe score >=3 or remediation plan attached
Clear upgrade window and rollback plan documented
Feasibility spike outcome (engineering) documented with LOE estimate
Assigned lane (Fast‑lane / Standard / Escalate) and next milestone date recorded
